questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience new culture and nature and get a different setting from what I am used to back home in Denmark. So, it was not only for the academic aspect I chose to go to Perth, but also for the personal experience and testing my own boundaries.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved it!! At first you had to get into it and get to know the others. And the weather was really terrible in the beginning. But after 1-2 months everything fell into place and I have met the nicest people and experienced what Western Australia has to offer - which is a lot.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was quite easy and they were very helpful when you wrote to the university (UWA) regarding any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is a intro week for all the exchange students, so you get to meet all the others who are in the same boat as you - thus it becomes easier to adjust and know what to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Many thing were sold out, if you looked for student accommodation outside of campus, so you had to be quick.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The student accommodations are good because other students live there... but I would recommend getting a room in a house. I wish I had done that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Boulevard wasn't that great, tbh

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They send you all the info and everything you need to do - so that is quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write to either the University in Copenhagen or the one you are going on exchange to - both are very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a bit of trouble getting the right conversion from the class in UWA to UCPH, because I took some classes which were the same as Micro and Macro 3 in Denmark. But when I wrote UCPH again, they changed it so I could get merit for it. But I got every class I wanted at UWA.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the unit outlines of the classes as it helps a lot with choosing which ones to choose.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The way the classes are feels a bit like high school as you get participation grades and have to say something in the classes. Also the level of the classes feels a bit lower than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Felt a bit lower than in Copenhagen, but it was good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was more like high school, which was a bit annoying as I enjoy the self study method in Denmark. 
And at UWA everything you do during the semester is going to reflect in your grade, as the assignments also count in the final grade - not just the actual exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Macroeconomic
Money, Banking and Financial Markets
Game Theory and Strategic Thinking
Environmental Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked them all actually - except the environmental economics, but I think that is just because it isn't my cup of tea.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Australia is very expensive in general, so just the cost of groceries and other necessities were quite a chok.. just as pricey if not more pricey than Copenhagen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: everything, but coffee and public transport is cheap - and cars are cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: many clubs and sports are available

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: joining some beginners sports which they offer exchange students is fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: buy a car and go on weekend trips and to the beach every time you can! It really pays of and you can sell it again afterwards.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quite easy. Australians are so nice

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: get a job

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: there are a lot of crazy people approaching you on the streets ://

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the nature and the nice people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get a job so you get to know Australians as you mostly get to know other exchange students at uni, buy a car so you can go on many roadtrips and bring warm clothes as it is colder than you expect in july/august/september

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: what I mentioned above is the most important

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the friends I have made and the experiences we have created together in Perth and on our trips

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: sometimes you have slumps and miss people at home, but it will go up and down - and mostly up!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: enjoy and have fun - school is important but the experiences made outside of school are the ones I will remember! And say yes to everything

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
